For context I’m a thirty six year old women, my sister is thirty four. My sister has three kids with her ex husband and I have four with my husband. This entire saga traumatized my younger sister and the divorce was rough. I’m completely disgusted with my ex brother in law and so is my entire inner family. We’ve completely cut contact with him. Ever since the whole divorce I don’t want my ex brother in law in my home. He’s no longer invited to any events. My sister was upset and said that her kids would be upset to not have their dad at big events like this. She said she hates him for cheating but accepts that she has kids with him so they are stuck together for life. But I have the right to not want someone I hate in my home and at my events. I stood by firmly and my husband agreed with me. Her kids got upset that I didn’t want their dad at any events and my kids now hate their ex uncle (even though I haven’t ever spoken to them about the situation). It was my daughters birthday this January and I was throwing a very extravagant party. I rented out an amusement park for the day and my daughters entire grade came. Parents of course as they are fourth graders and my sisters son wanted his father there and of course I let him know my rule stands. My sister got upset and says that she can fight her own battles and that banning him makes me an asshole. My sister has always allowed this guy to walk all over her and always defends him. Am I wrong for not wanting him at events and parties I throw? I just don’t see it.

He cheated on her with multiple women and even impregnated two others, both of whom had abortions. This whole situation was really traumatic for my younger sister, and the divorce was tough on her. I, along with the rest of our family, am completely disgusted with him and have cut off all contact. Only my sister still communicates with him, which is something I don't really understand. I host a lot of family events at my houseâĢĶbirthdays, Easter, Christmas parties, and so on. Since the divorce, I've made it clear that I don't want my ex-brother-in-law in my home or at any of these events. My husband supports this decision, and we've been consistent about it. However, my sister has been upset about this. She says that her kids would be upset if their dad isn't at big events like these. She hates him for cheating but acknowledges that they have kids together, so they're stuck together for life. I get that part, but I still don't see why I should have someone I hate in my home and at my events. I've stood firm on this, and my husband agrees with me. Then, during my daughter's birthday party this January, which was a really big event where I rented out an amusement park and invited her entire fourth-grade class and their parents, my sister's son wanted his father there. I let him know that my rule still stands. My sister got upset and called me a asshole for banning him. She also said she can fight her own battles, implying that I shouldn't be involved in this decision. I'm confused now. Am I wrong for not wanting him at these events? I just don't see it. I want to protect my family and create a safe environment for my kids, but I also don't want to cause unnecessary drama or hurt my sister's feelings. Maybe I should consider why my sister is so insistent on having him around. Is it because she feels guilty or maybe she still has some unresolved feelings towards him? Or is it because she genuinely believes that her kids need to have a relationship with their father despite his actions? On the other hand, I have to think about the impact this has on my own kids. If I allow him to come to our events, would that send the wrong message to my children about what's acceptable behavior? I want them to grow up knowing that cheating and infidelity are not acceptable, and that people who do such things shouldn't be welcomed into our lives. But then again, my sister's kids are also my niece and nephew. They deserve to have a relationship with their father, even if he's not a good person. Or do they? Is it better for them to have no contact with him to protect them from his negative influence? I'm also thinking about the practical aspects. If I allow him to come, would he cause drama or make things uncomfortable for everyone? I don't want to risk that, especially since I've worked hard to create a positive and enjoyable environment for our family events. Maybe there's a middle ground. Could we have events where he's allowed to attend under certain conditions, or maybe have separate events where the kids can see him without him being around our family? I'm not sure if that's feasible, though. I also wonder if there's a way to communicate this to my sister without causing more conflict. She seems to be taking this personally, and I don't want to damage our relationship over this. But I also can't compromise on something that I feel strongly about. In the end, I need to decide what's best for my family and what aligns with my values. I don't want to let someone who has caused so much pain into our space, but I also don't want to be the reason my sister or her kids are upset. It's a tough situation, and I'm not sure what the right decision is.
